title: I and You
hook: Martin Buber taught two ways of meeting the world: as an "it", or as a "you"
carry: every true you opens onto the eternal you
tomorrow: why would someone travel just to watch a rabbi tie his shoes?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Rav Kook and the late-night ache: the soul is always praying, and the longing is part of it. The soul longs. Today, a different kind of reaching: toward the person right in front of you.

At rehearsal, Noa's scene partner says every line to a spot just past her ear. Technically perfect. She feels like a lamp he happens to be standing near. That's the answer to yesterday's question, and the philosopher Martin Buber built a small book around it. Say "it" to someone and they become something to use, sort or get past. Say "you" and something else starts. Now the puzzle. Buber's book, I and Thou, is about God. So why does it stop, early on, to look hard at a tree?
screen: `LINES SAID PAST HER EAR.` → `IT, OR YOU?` → `A BOOK ABOUT GOD... AND A TREE?`

segments.voice: Start with Buber's claim. There are two basic words, and each is a pair: I-It and I-You. There's no I standing alone. The I who measures and uses is a different I from the one who meets. Buber doesn't call It evil. He says nobody can live without it; we need schedules, tools and facts. But a person who lives with It alone, he says, isn't fully human. Now the tree. Buber says he can look at a tree as a picture, a type of plant, a set of laws about water and light. All true, all It. And yet, he writes, it can happen that he's drawn into relation with that tree, and it's no longer an object. It's a You. That's the puzzle solved. The You isn't saved for God or for great loves. It's a way of meeting anything, starting with whatever's nearest. And then Buber's turn: every You we meet is a glimpse through to what he calls the eternal You. A book about God opens on a tree because, for Buber, that's where the road to God begins. One fact to tell a friend: his German word was Du, the word for someone close, which is why some translators prefer "you" to the stiff old "thou".
screen: `TWO WORDS: I-IT AND I-YOU.` · `NOBODY LIVES WITHOUT IT.` · `EVEN A TREE CAN BE A YOU.` · `EVERY YOU OPENS ON THE ETERNAL YOU.` · then, large: `MEET THE YOU.`

segments.voice: Pick up your phone and choose one person you'll see this week. Write them a single line that's only about them: not a plan, not a favor, just something you've noticed and like. Send it, or save it for when you see them.
Meet the you: Martin Buber's teaching that we can treat the world as It, to use, or meet it as You, whole and present.
Here's the line: every true you opens onto the eternal you. For Buber, the road to God starts with whoever's nearest.

howItsDone: Buber's I and Thou is read in Jewish adult study, in university courses and by readers of many faiths; his language of I-It and I-You is often used in teaching about prayer, marriage and friendship.

fork.setup: your mom asks how the new coworker is. you realize all you know is his job title and that he's slow on email. what would Buber point at?
options: so far he's only been an It: a role and a speed. meet him once.

fork.reveal: Buber says we all need It, but anyone, even a tree, can become a You. the coworker hasn't been met yet.

original.note: Hebrew: you (to one man). Buber's book in Hebrew is called Ani ve-Atah, I and You.

trapdoor: what you thought: I and Thou sounds like old church English about God.

what a scholar hears: the German Ich und Du, where Du is the close, familiar word, so 'Thou' can sound more formal than Buber meant.

chat.says: scene partner says every line to the wall behind me. i feel like set dressing. how do i fix it
options: Meet him first, offstage. Ask what the scene means to him; then you're a you, not a prop.
Play past him to the audience too. If he won't look at you, nobody notices anyway.
Tell the director to fix his eyeline. Blocking notes will solve it faster than talking.
chat.meaning: Buber says another person can be an It, something to get past, or a You, met whole. Meeting usually starts with a real question, not a fix.

tie.story: Martin Buber wrote that even a tree can be met as a You, and every true You opens onto the eternal You, God.
tie.friend: Noa can meet her scene partner as a You offstage, so onstage they are two people, not a voice and a prop.
tie.you: who have you been treating as an It lately?
